Maintenance Report — MNT-0182-007

Asset: WELL-0182 (NE-08 Well 182, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 06 Apr 2024 08:00 · Finished: 30 Apr 2024 20:00 · Well stopped for this job: 588 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Kevin Price · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0182-0075 on 2024-04-04 Report written: 30 Apr 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the pumper heard grinding from the walking beam and saw the horsehead wobbling. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0182-0075 showed the wellhead at 20.0 °C with the air at 17.7 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 22 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

Root cause

Bearing wear from long service and an overdue grease interval.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

Parts and cost

Bolts, shims and seals435

Labour (company crew and contractor)2,942
Total5,840

Notes and recommendations

  • Shorten the grease interval on this unit to 60 days.
  • Check saddle bearings on neighbouring units of the same age.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0182-010

Asset: WELL-0182 (NE-08 Well 182, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: downhole pump Work started: 02 Aug 2024 08:00 · Finished: 07 Aug 2024 18:00 · Well stopped for this job: 130 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Megan Ward · Contractor: Sandstone Rod & Pump Triggered by: inspection INS-0182-0091 on 2024-08-01 Report written: 09 Aug 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the wellhead was cold and the pump jack was straining with a heavy, uneven load. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0182-0091 showed the wellhead at 40.7 °C with the air at 36.5 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The downhole pump was stuck, most likely from sand or scale. Sandstone Rod & Pump's workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 3 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

A worn plunger that let sand settle and lock the pump.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 4 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rods and the insert pump.
  3. Inspected the pump: sand in the barrel and a worn plunger.
  4. Ran in a new insert pump.
  5. Re-spaced the pump and hung the rods back on.

Summary of the fix: pulled and replaced downhole pump.

Testing and return to service

Pump test confirmed fluid to surface and the wellhead warmed back to normal. The well was returned to production.

Parts and cost

Rig services2,955
Consumables1,182
Labour (company crew and contractor)7,121
Total18,941

Compliance check

  • Review sand control on this well.
  • Send the old pump for teardown.

What happened

Field staff reported that the electric motor driving the pump jack had stopped and would not restart. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0182-0109 showed the wellhead at 13.3 °C with the air at 7.9 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well stayed shut in for about 21 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

Winding breakdown from heat and age.

Safety and permits

Maintenance Report — MNT-0182-020

Asset: WELL-0182 (NE-08 Well 182, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: flowline Work started: 16 Jan 2026 08:00 · Finished: 16 Jan 2026 20:00 · Well stopped for this job: 12 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Megan Ward · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0182-0164 on 2026-01-15 Report written: 17 Jan 2026

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0182-0164 at 13:00 on 2026-01-15 found crude oil on the pad: about 11.2% of the pad area, estimated 5.9 bbl. The inspector noted: "Oil sheen around cellar." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 3.0 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to the flanged flowline connection at the wellhead cellar.

Root cause

A failed gasket on the flange where the flowline leaves the wellhead.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Cleaned free oil out of the cellar.
  2. Unbolted the flange and removed the failed gasket.
  3. Fitted a new gasket and new bolts, torqued to specification.
  4. Excavated the stained soil around the cellar.

Summary of the fix: replaced the flange gasket and bolts and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 251 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 201 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 3.9 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0182-020 (WS-06).
  • 4 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.51% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Parts and cost

ItemUSD
Flange gasket and bolts442
Absorbents and berms885
Soil hauling and disposal1,622
Labour (company crew and contractor)2,134
Total5,083

Compliance check

ProtocolResultDetail

WS-02MetEnergy isolated and tagged
WS-03MetMonitors bump-tested; highest 2 ppm
WS-05MetTested at 1.25 × maximum operating pressure, held 4 hours
WS-06MetOily waste manifested to an approved site
WS-07MetWritten 1 day after the work (limit 3 days)
SR-02MetContained about 3.0 hours after discovery (limit 4 hours)
SR-01MetWritten notice filed with the State Oil & Gas Commission 2 hours after discovery (limit 24 hours)
SR-03In progressCleaned to below 1.0% TPH; agency verification requested (due within 60 days of discovery)
SR-04MetSpill recorded with volume and area (reportable class)

Notes and recommendations

  • Inspect the remaining joints on this flowline.
  • Record the leak location for the flowline maintenance program (RC-05).
